records.reason: m141 at 10/1 and 138 mg fills the fixed-loading gap between measured 5/1 (65f4f125b5e1f8137bd9: 16.38/46.42 mL) and 20/1 (51f4126a3aadb3239225: 43.47/118.59 mL). It tests where the steep response develops after the historical plateau prediction failed.

m141 at 10/1 and 46 mg directly contrasts with the selected 138 mg row. Their current predictions are nearly identical, so this measures whether loading changes onset or completion in the newly identified long-retention region.
m141 at 5/1 and 46 mg completes a 5/1-to-10/1, two-loading rectangle using measured 65f4f125b5e1f8137bd9. This distinguishes a loading-dependent response slope from a simple molecular correction.

m94 at 5/1 and 176.1 mg bridges measured 1/1 d549eb843e65b16a5502 and 20/1 ffffcd6f3b9393846ab4. The latter had 38.18 mL historical V2 underprediction; this point tests the beginning of the revised steep curve.

m94 at 10/1 matches the selected 5/1 and measured 20/1 loading and injection conditions. Its predicted 23.58/55.53 mL endpoints test whether retraining learned the response shape or mainly adjusted the measured weak-eluent endpoint.

m94 at 20/1 and 58.7 mg provides a threefold loading contrast to ffffcd6f3b9393846ab4 at fixed injection volume. The current prediction remains near the high-loading result, making this a direct test of transfer across loading.

m27 at 20/1 and 52.85 mg tests the interior of the unexpectedly flat measured 2/1-to-50/1 response in 504e8e25f3a8b339a023 and 55927e904f7c540fd4f2. It can distinguish a broadly early-eluting scaffold from an unusual endpoint observation.

m27 at 50/1 and 105.7 mg doubles loading relative to 55927e904f7c540fd4f2 while holding injection conditions fixed. It checks whether the large historical overprediction was repaired in a way that generalizes beyond the original loading.
m125 at 5/1, 150 mg, and 500 uL DCM directly contrasts with measured 549daca56bed1c9d2bcc at 300 uL. This tests whether the injection-volume differences observed at 1/1 and 2/1 persist at 5/1.

m125 in pure EA, 100 mg, and 500 uL DCM matches measured e7ed7ca4a53258b73ba2 at 300 uL. This strong-eluent control tests whether the injection-volume association disappears when mobile-phase strength increases.

m202 at 10/1 and 183.45 mg extends the measured loading series: 7de812bda21b4dfe46dc gave 14.79/21.41 mL at 61.15 mg, versus 35.08/70.35 mL at 122.3 mg in 902937db42f82f467718. It tests whether that difference continues, saturates, or reflects unexplained variability.

m72 at 10/1 and 51.1 mg fills the exact-condition gap between 10f01f359bc6067d009f at 5/1 and 1b1a9ec85268aa66d327 at 20/1. The predicted 27.74/83.44 mL endpoints and wide V1 quantile span make the placement of this transition a useful learning target.

Unmeasured m29 at 5/1 and 97.5 mg anchors a sterically crowded aromatic ketone. Its two ortho methyl groups provide a focused structural contrast to measured acetophenone derivatives without assuming that steric shielding determines retention.

m29 at 50/1 matches the selected 5/1 conditions. Measuring the predicted change from about 5.90/12.69 to 8.14/27.82 mL tests whether the model transfers carbonyl accessibility and solvent sensitivity to this crowded environment.

Unmeasured methyl-substituted tetralone m63 at 10/1 anchors a cyclic aromatic ketone series. The selected m180 points and measured larger-ring ketone m179 offer related structures for testing local ring-environment transfer.

m63 at 20/1 matches its selected 10/1 conditions and the eluent ratio of measured m179 record 8b59c86480a0a3337c63. This tests a modest predicted response rather than assuming all carbonyl compounds have steep weak-eluent retention.

Unmeasured tetralone m180 at 10/1 and 109.9 mg provides the unsubstituted counterpart to m63. Its high similarity to observed chemistry makes this a test of local generalization, not merely structural novelty.

m180 at 20/1 completes the same 10/1-to-20/1 ratio contrast selected for m63. Together with m179 observation 8b59c86480a0a3337c63, these labels constrain how ring size and methyl substitution modify the two endpoints.

Unmeasured meta-fluoropropiophenone m65 at 2/1 and 107.4 mg anchors a close chemical transfer test from bromopropiophenone m64 and fluorinated acetophenones. This separates a new molecular offset from the selected solvent-response contrast.

m65 at 20/1 matches its selected 2/1 loading and injection conditions. Its predicted 10.79/22.92 mL endpoints test whether the model transfers substitution and side-chain effects across the recurring aromatic-ketone family.

Unmeasured primary alcohol m204 at 2/1 and 150.15 mg anchors a flexible phenylpropyl scaffold. It provides a focused comparison with secondary and tertiary alcohols, where measured retention is not explained by the presence of OH alone.

m204 at 10/1 matches the selected 2/1 conditions and tests the predicted rise to 30.66/54.54 mL. This measures whether the steep response learned from other alcohols transfers to a primary OH separated from the aromatic ring.

Unmeasured secondary alcohol m60 at 2/1 and 97 mg supplies a stronger-eluent anchor for a structural bridge between benzylic alcohol m67 and tertiary alcohol m51. This makes its weaker-eluent label interpretable as a response slope.

m60 at 10/1 matches its selected 2/1 conditions. The predicted 31.51/50.09 mL endpoints test transfer of OH environment and linker effects after the substantial historical underprediction of m67 in db5dcc7b864e0174fcbd.

m166 at 10/1 and 150 mg extends beyond its measured pure-EA anchor 14d7f6fb3dda38f48fb9. It anchors the selected weak-eluent contrast for a fluorinated aromatic beta-diketone, a different environment from the recently corrected beta-ketoesters.

m166 at 50/1 matches its selected 10/1 conditions. Predicted endpoints rise from about 7.07/16.93 to 38.19/71.97 mL; this substantial unmeasured curvature and high CW distance justify testing the transfer directly.

m167 at 50/1 and 150 mg is the phenyl analogue of selected naphthyl m166. Its much smaller predicted endpoints, 16.41/32.38 mL, test whether the model's large aromatic-extension effect is real; bd4a842f0d21e901f024 supplies its measured pure-EA anchor.

m87 at 20/1 and 55.15 mg extends the exact loading series beyond measured 10/1 record 8b197f0ed5860f909b5f at 8.46/19.70 mL. The predicted 24.06/38.28 mL endpoints test a sharp increase in an aromatic ester with a methoxy group.

m87 at 50/1 matches the selected 20/1 conditions and tests the further predicted increase to 40.72/67.57 mL. High CW distance and a crossed V1 quantile ordering reinforce the need for a label, without establishing that the prediction is wrong.

Phenylmalonate m75 at 50/1 and 54.75 mg extends measured 20/1 record 3726956d81fe3954e5b7, which gave 18.43/30.51 mL. The predicted 33.07/60.35 mL endpoints test weak-eluent transfer in a diester and help distinguish it from beta-ketoesters.

Oxime m11 at 20/1 and 100 mg follows measured 10/1 record 6b5982c6e1bbaadd6a95, where V2 was historically overpredicted by 44.45 mL. It tests whether the current model now places the onset of stronger retention correctly.

m11 at 50/1 matches the selected 20/1 conditions. Its predicted 28.12/76.53 mL endpoints test whether the revised oxime curve genuinely becomes steep at weaker eluent or still carries an exaggerated completion response.

hypotheses.content: 2,6-Lutidine has a steep recorded solvent-response curve between 5/1 and 20/1; steric shielding around nitrogen did not produce the previously predicted plateau. Whether the curve depends on loading remains unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The historical V2 error at 20/1 was about -79 mL. Intermediate and crossed-loading labels can teach a response shape rather than only an endpoint correction, with relevance to other basic heteroaromatics.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 10/1, where does the increase occur, and does the 5/1-to-10/1 slope differ between 46 and 138 mg?

hypotheses.content: Dicarbonyl and multi-ester response curves depend strongly on local structure. The steep measured curves of m94, m78, and m82 should not be transferred uniformly to aromatic beta-diketones or diesters.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Functional-group counts alone cannot explain the supplied endpoints. Response and analogue contrasts can improve learned interactions between carbonyl environment and eluent strength.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m94 show a smooth intermediate response, and are the large predicted weak-eluent differences among m166, m167, and m75 supported by measurement?

hypotheses.content: Recorded loading amount and injection volume can have molecule- and ratio-dependent associations with V1/V2 that the current predictions nearly ignore. The m125 injection-volume association and m202 loading association require separate tests and do not establish a universal causal rule.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched contrasts can expose condition interactions that would otherwise be absorbed into molecular offsets. Unrecorded variables and observational variability limit mechanistic attribution.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m125 retain an injection-volume difference at 5/1 or in pure EA, and does m202's 10/1 response continue changing at higher loading?

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl-containing compounds cannot be assigned a common solvent-response slope. m27 remains early-eluting at both measured ratios, while aromatic and cyclic ketones provide distinct environments whose transfer should be tested locally.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The m27 failure shows that a chemically plausible carbonyl prior can still yield a large prediction error. Matched curves across crowded, cyclic, and substituted ketones can refine structural features that generalize across many catalog rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m27 remain early-eluting at an intermediate ratio and higher loading, and do m29, m63, m180, and m65 follow their predicted local response slopes?

hypotheses.content: Alcohol response transfer depends on OH placement and surrounding structure. A steep response is plausible for m60 and m204, but the heterogeneous measured alcohol examples do not establish it.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Primary, secondary, benzylic, and more remote alcohol environments offer a focused test of whether the graph representation captures adsorption differences beyond an OH indicator.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m60 and m204 show the predicted large 2/1-to-10/1 increases under fixed loading conditions?

hypotheses.content: The current oxime m11 curve may still place excessive growth in completion volume at weak eluent after correcting its earlier 10/1 overprediction; alternatively, its steep response may begin only beyond 10/1.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Measuring two weaker-eluent points distinguishes a persistent scaffold-specific error from a misplaced transition and constrains V1 and V2 separately.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the predicted 20/1 and 50/1 endpoints consistent with the measured 10/1 anchor of 10.08/23.96 mL?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes reject the previous lutidine plateau prediction: m141 at 20/1 measured 43.47/118.59 mL, with historical errors of -23.62/-79.19 mL. They also reject the predicted strong solvent sensitivity of m27 at the measured loading: its endpoints were 5.75/8.99 mL at 2/1 and 5.81/7.34 mL at 50/1. Conversely, m94 at 20/1 and m99 at 10/1 had substantial historical underprediction, supporting structure-specific response follow-up rather than a single correction for all carbonyl or OH compounds. The m78 curve now has several measured anchors, and its two 50/1 loading levels gave similar completion volumes; its marginal value is lower than the unresolved m94 transition. The m125 1/1 contrast strengthens the injection-volume association: 300 versus 500 uL DCM gave 7.50/20.47 versus 13.44/38.40 mL at 100 mg, although the direction and magnitude across ratios remain unresolved. Recent m90 and m198 results were relatively close to their acquisition predictions, reducing priority for nearby rows. I use the observed table as authoritative where memory conflicts: d7457b516ddba0143275 is recorded there as m94 in pure EA at 176.1 mg, not as an m21 2/1 measurement. These are acquisition-time errors and measured contrasts, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The batch connects failure repair to transferable experiments. Lutidine receives a ratio/loading rectangle, m94 receives intermediate points and a loading contrast, and m27 receives an interior-ratio check plus a higher-loading weak-eluent test. The m125 and m202 selections directly examine recorded condition effects that current predictions represent as nearly negligible. New ketone and alcohol pairs test specific structural relationships across recurring catalog families, with moderate predicted retention included alongside steeper curves. Fluorinated beta-diketone analogues, methoxybenzoate, phenylmalonate, and oxime probe weak-eluent relationships that remain poorly anchored. Multiple rows for one molecule are retained when they identify slopes or condition interactions; duplicate condition rows are not added merely because they have different IDs. Quantile spans are single-predictor output spans, not calibrated epistemic uncertainty, and elution interval width is not treated as uncertainty. Labels from this batch should help retraining distinguish molecular offsets, solvent-response curvature, and loading interactions across the Row-distribution. Missing experimental variables and occasional inconsistent observations prevent confident causal interpretation or a guarantee of improvement.
